newsitem.title: UK: Dollar soars on German jobless worries.
newsitem.headline: Dollar soars on German jobless worries.

text.p: The dollar soared to a two-year high against the mark on Wednesday, driven by fears of poor German jobless figures later this week and new anxiety over Russian president Boris Yeltsin's health.

In equity markets, stocks made healthy gains helped initially by Wall Street's overnight record close. And Wednesday's unsteady opening in New York failed to make much of a dent on this side of the Atlantic.
The dollar hit its two-year peak of 1.5747 marks, more than a pfennig up on levels seen late on Tuesday, before falling back slightly in afternoon trading.

"It's been helped this morning by rumours about Yeltsin's health, and I think there's also some buying sparked by expectations of weak German unemployment data coming in tomorrow," said David Brown, chief European economist at Bear Stearns.
Yeltsin spent Wednesday at his country residence outside Moscow nursing a heavy cold but the surgeon who gave him a multiple heart bypass two months ago said there was no cause for alarm.

Jitters over the upcoming German jobless statistics due on Thursday were undermining the mark because poor figures could increase pressure for interest rate cuts, making the mark less attractive to currency investors.
"It (weaker German jobs data) could spark more rate cut speculation, and that's going to build up ahead of the Bundesbank council meeting tomorrow," said Bear Stearns' Brown.
The Bundesbank's policy-making council is due to hold its first regular meeting of the year on Thursday.
The dollar was also stronger on the yen, testing the 116 level. But traders said the rise was a correction after the dollar's recent weakness against the Japanese currency.
London, Europe's biggest stock exchange, climbed 0.2 percent after losses on Tuesday. Business, however, was cautious because of interest rate anxiety and Wall Street's recent volatility.
"People are starting to worry that interest rates may be pushed up sooner rather than later," one senior dealer said.

Market talk of higher British interest rates intensified after the deputy governor of the Bank of England late on Tuesday said there was a need for a small rate rise to achieve the government's inflation target.
Other European bourses put on more robust performances but the mood was nervous because of worries that record-breaking levels of recent weeks could not be sustained much longer.

Nerves were not helped by a disappointing opening in New York on Wednesday after closing at a record level in the previous session. Wall Street ended up 33.48 points at 6,600.66 on Tuesday, surpassing Monday's peak of 6,567.18.
The Dow Jones industrials were down 0.25 percent on Wednesday after an opening rise. Analysts said the market was worried about the chance of higher interest rates.
French stocks were the strongest climbers, holding gains of over one percent despite Wall Street's downturn.
Brokers said investors were bullish but also cautious ahead of two important U.S. indicators due out on Thursday and Friday, the December producer price index and non-farm payrolls.
In Frankfurt, stocks ended floor trade up 0.7 percent, boosted by the strengthening dollar, which improved prospects for German exporters, and the positive debt market.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5717 marks and 115.72 yen compared with 1.5634 and 115.25 in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1545 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of key British shares was 7.0 points higher at 4,085.8.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up up 20.21 at 2,906.34.
In Paris, the CAC-40 index was up 28.73 at 2,330.42.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $356.60, well below Tuesday's London close of $359.35. Silver was at $4.66, down six cents.
